result.title: Unlocking Fine-Grained Cell Representations via Soft-Interior Rim Dense-Grid Pooling in Pathology Foundation Models
result.summary: Fine-grained cell representations are essential for characterizing cellular heterogeneity and tissue organization in computational pathology. Pathology foundation models (PFMs) provide powerful pretrained features for transferable tissue analysis. HoVer-Net uses task-trained segmentation and typing, whereas CellViT++ averages native-grid tokens assigned to detected nuclei. However, the former requires cell-specific training; the latter ignores fractional nuclear coverage and can mix nuclear content with neighbouring tissue. Therefore, we propose SRDP, short for Soft-interior Rim Dense-grid Pooling, a training-free geometry-aware readout. We apply the frozen patch projection at half stride, interleave four offset lattices, map the cell mask to fractional coverage weights, and concatenate whole-cell pooling with two inner boundary pools. Across four datasets and six frozen encoders, SRDP improves mean balanced accuracy by 5.68 percentage points over native token averaging across 24 settings, including 11.22 points on average for CoNIC and Lizard. SRDP converts a coarse frozen PFM lattice into a mask-aligned, fine-grained cell representation without updating the encoder.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 SRDP，一种免训练的几何感知读出方式：以半步长应用冻结的 patch 投影并交错四个偏移格点，将细胞掩膜映射为分数覆盖权重，再把整体细胞池化与两个内边界池化拼接，用于从病理基础模型中提取细粒度细胞表示。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按掩膜分数覆盖重加权、避免混入邻近组织」的读出思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与细节保留问题，即如何从冻结视觉特征中按区域对齐地取出任务必要信息；但原文并不涉及 latent 推理或多模态生成。
